title: Binding site plasticity regulation of the FimH catch-bond mechanism
authors: Olivier Languin–Cattoën; Fabio Sterpone; Guillaume Stirnemann
one_liner_zh: 该文用增强采样MD研究细菌黏附素FimH的catch-bond机制，聚焦蛋白-糖类互作而非蛋白-DNA，虽涉及结合位点动态与力调控，但对象和方法均与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: The bacterial fimbrial adhesin FimH is a remarkable and well-studied catch-bond protein found at the tip of E. coli type 1 pili, which allows pathogenic strains involved in urinary tract infections to bind high-mannose glycans exposed on human epithelia. The catch-bond behavior of FimH, where the strength of the interaction increases when a force is applied to separate the two partners, enables the bacteria to resist clearance when they are subjected to shear forces induced by urine flow. Two decades of experimental studies performed at the single-molecule level, as well as X-ray crystallography and modeling studies, have led to a consensus picture whereby force separates the binding domain from an inhibitor domain, effectively triggering an allosteric conformational change in the former. This force-induced allostery is thought to be responsible for an increased binding affinity at the core of the catch-bond mechanism. However, some important questions remain, the most challenging one being that the crystal structures corresponding to these two allosteric states show almost superimposable binding-site geometries, which questions the molecular origin for the large difference in affinity. Using molecular dynamics with a combination of enhanced-sampling techniques, we demonstrate that the static picture provided by the crystal structures conceals a variety of binding-site conformations that have a key impact on the apparent affinity. Crucially, the respective populations in each of these conformations are very different between the two allosteric states of the binding domain, which can then be related to experimental affinity measurements. We also evidence a previously unappreciated but important effect: in addition to the well-established role of the force as an allosteric regulator via domain separation, application of force tends to directly favor the high-affinity binding-site conformations. We hypothesize that this additional local catch-bond effect could delay unbinding between the bacteria and the host cell before the global allosteric transition occurs, as well as stabilizing the complex even more once in the high-affinity allosteric state.
abstract_zh: 细菌性菌毛黏附素FimH是一种显著且被广泛研究的catch-bond蛋白，位于大肠杆菌1型菌毛尖端，使涉及尿路感染的致病菌株能够结合人类上皮细胞表面暴露的高甘露糖聚糖。FimH的catch-bond行为，即当施加力以分离两个结合伙伴时相互作用强度增加，使细菌在受到尿液流动诱导的剪切力时能够抵抗清除。二十年来在单分子水平进行的实验研究，以及X射线晶体学和建模研究，已形成共识性图景：力将结合域与抑制域分离，有效触发前者的变构构象变化。这种力诱导的变构被认为是在catch-bond机制核心处增加结合亲和力的原因。然而，一些重要问题仍然存在，最具挑战性的是，对应于这两个变构状态的晶体结构显示出几乎可叠加的结合位点几何形状，这对亲和力巨大差异的分子起源提出了疑问。利用分子动力学结合增强采样技术，我们证明晶体结构提供的静态图景掩盖了多种结合位点构象，这些构象对表观亲和力具有关键影响。至关重要的是，每种构象中的各自群体在结合域的两个变构状态之间差异显著，这随后可与实验亲和力测量相关联。我们还揭示了一个先前未被重视但重要的效应：除了力作为通过域分离实现的变构调节器的既定作用外，施加力倾向于直接有利于高亲和力结合位点构象。我们假设这种额外的局部catch-bond效应可能在全局变构转变发生前延迟细菌与宿主细胞之间的解离，并且一旦处于高亲和力变构状态，还能进一步稳定复合物。
